narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model predicts that you have a 21% chance of not passing your final year. Because this probability is above the school’s threshold of 10%, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your academic progress.

The prediction was shaped most strongly by three factors. First, your record shows no previous class failures, which is actually a positive sign—most students in your situation also have no past failures, and this helped lower your risk of not passing. Second, your strong desire to pursue higher education also worked in your favor, as every student aiming for further studies tends to be more motivated, and this reduced your risk as well.

However, the factor that increased your risk the most was your long daily commute to school, which is over an hour each way. Only about 3% of students in your peer group have such a lengthy travel time, and this can make it harder to keep up with schoolwork and stay engaged, especially compared to the majority who live much closer.

While some aspects of your profile suggest you are well-prepared, the challenge of your long commute means you may face additional obstacles. Taking remedial courses is intended to give you extra support and resources, helping you overcome these challenges and succeed in your final year. It’s important to make the most of this opportunity and seek help if you find your travel time is affecting your studies.
